patch_description: Replace the current single-block, densely-parametrized ansatz (which scored lower, 0.85 combined) with the more successful modular two-block design (previously validated at 0.89 combined / 0.90 test accuracy), and apply the recommended refinement: partially de-share the nearest-neighbor ring CRZ parameters across the two block copies. Concretely, the first block gets its own `crz_ring_even_b0`/`crz_ring_odd_b0` ring parameters, while the second block keeps the base `crz_ring_even`/`crz_ring_odd` names. All other layers (RY/RX single-qubit rotations, skip-2, skip-3, and diameter CRZ entanglers) remain fully shared across both blocks, exactly as in the strong modular seed. This adds only 2 extra trainable parameters relative to full sharing, giving each block slightly more local-mixing flexibility while preserving the strong regularization from sharing the bulk of parameters (RY/RX single-qubit layers and all longer-range entanglers). This should recover the higher validation/test accuracy and lower generalization gap seen in the modular seed, while testing whether asymmetric ring flexibility yields a further accuracy boost.
